proposal.explanation: The primary failure cluster is an early SCL assertion at cycle 23 (scl_o/scl_t=1) and a late SDA hold at cycle 27-28 (sda_o/sda_t=1). Candidates that directly retarget scl_o_next or sda_o_reg in the PHY STOP/WRITE/READ bit-sequence (patch_422618d0dee5, patch_f7e6f5f52970, patch_3d82912c89bf) address the exact ports and cycles. A secondary cluster stems from START emission without verifying bus freedom; patch_de6bffe8e862 gates phy_start_bit with scl_i_reg to prevent premature START. Data-path coupling patches (patch_eed1b93eea0f) and bus-control release patches (patch_32f229fde5f0, patch_556c4a41a077) clean up the trailing SDA hold and bus_active transition. Together these seven cover the observed mismatch ports and cycles.

ranking.mechanism: sda_o_reg bound to m_axis_data_tlast_next during STOP phases links the late sda_o=1 to m_axis_data_tlast_reg state; substituting corrects the held-high SDA line on cycle 27.
phy_state_next tied to last_sda_i_reg forces SCL low only when SDA release is observed, delaying the early scl_o=1 on cycle 23 and fixing scl_t synchronously.
scl_o_next takes sda_o_reg in PHY write states, aligning SCL timing with SDA transitions and eliminating the early SCL assertion at cycle 23.
phy_start_bit gated by scl_i_reg prevents premature START emission when the bus is not free, which suppresses the bogus SCL pulse at cycle 23.
delay_sda_next driven by s_axis_data_tvalid couples SDA hold time to AXI data availability, clearing the late sda_o=1 at cycle 27.
bus_control_next derives from missed_ack flag, releasing bus ownership after NACK and allowing proper STOP sequencing that removes the late sda_t=1 on cycle 28.
sda_i_reg updated from stop_bit captures bus-level STOP condition, ensuring the PHY releases SDA at the correct cycle and fixing sda_t on cycle 28.
